nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $H_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k$ be the $n$-th harmonic number. Then $x \cos^n x \sin(nx)$ and $\cos^n x \sin(nx)$ are integrable on $[0, \pi/2]$, $\int_0^{\pi/2} x \cos^n x \sin(nx)\,dx = \frac{\pi}{2^{n+2}} H_n$ and $\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos^n x \sin(nx)\,dx = \frac{1}{2^{n+1}} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{2^k}{k}$.
nodes.title: Ramanujan's integrals of $\cos^n x \sin nx$ (Entry 33)

nodes.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and let $H_n = \sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k$ be the $n$-th harmonic number. Then $x \cos^n x \sin(nx)$ and $\cos^n x \sin(nx)$ are integrable on $[0, \pi/2]$, $\int_0^{\pi/2} x \cos^n x \sin(nx)\,dx = \frac{\pi}{2^{n+2}} H_n$ and $\int_0^{\pi/2} \cos^n x \sin(nx)\,dx = \frac{1}{2^{n+1}} \sum_{k=1}^{n} \frac{2^k}{k}$.
